references.text: In the previous chapter (John 9:32-33), witnesses argue that no one can open the eyes of a man born blind unless he is from God. This is the direct context for the debate in 10:21, where some use precisely this miracle as evidence against Jesus being possessed.

Verses 19-20 describe the same division among the Jews that leads to the discussion in verse 21. Here, Jesus is explicitly accused of being possessed by a demon (daimonion), which is the central point that the opposing side in verse 21 attempts to refute.

In this early chapter, the Jews accuse Jesus of being a Samaritan and possessed by a demon. Jesus responds by defending himself against the charge of having a demon, a theme that is resumed and discussed further in 10:21.

Here the crowd asks if Jesus is possessed by a demon, while others defend him. This early accusation of possession creates a recurring motif in the Gospel of John that culminates in the discussion about miracles in chapter 10.
